title: Introduce nonblocking trace hooks and metadata minifier to cut hotpath overhead
creator: Lena Park
description: Problem: Our instrumented hotpaths (inference gateway + SDK) still do span allocation and attribute serialization for nearly every request. This contributes measurable CPU and allocation pressure at high QPS, and increases jitter on p95/p99 latencies. Goal: reduce hotpath cost of tracing hooks by introducing a thin nonblocking shim that returns an opaque trace handle early, and by aggressively minifying span metadata at the callsite so expensive fields are dropped/deflated before they hit the tracer subsystem. Deliverables: 1) A lightweight runtime hook (C++/Rust shim) that avoids allocations on the hotpath and writes a fixed-size record to a lock-free ring buffer. 2) A background minifier/collector that expands and samples spans asynchronously, runs tail-retention heuristics, and emits sampled spans to the tracing backend. 3) New observability metrics and runtime knobs (feature flag + per-route opt-in) to rollout safely. 4) Integration tests and a performance regression harness. Why different from previous sampling efforts: instead of prefiltering decisions in the tracer or doing expensive checks inline, this approach moves a minimal footprint token creation into the hotpath and defers heavy work. Metadata minification reduces downstream encoding cost, and background tail-retention gives us a pragmatic way to keep interesting traces without inflating steady-state traffic.
comments: 2026-02-13 - Lena Park: Kickoff sync with runtime and tracer teams. Agreed to prototype a ring-buffer shim in the gateway and a Go-based background worker for early experiments. Action: Ravi to prototype hotpath shim; Asha to draft minification rules.

2026-02-20 - Ravi Patel: Prototype implemented in the gateway (native shim) and bench harness added. Hotpath now writes a 24-byte record to ring buffer instead of allocating a Span object. Synthetic load (100k rps) shows ~12% CPU reduction and 30% fewer allocations.

2026-02-27 - Design review: Decided minifier ruleset v0 to drop: raw request body, full cookie headers, duplicate http headers, and trace instrumentation keys used only for routing. We will keep top-k semantic tags (route, model_id, tenant) and a truncated request fingerprint. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Trace+Minifier+Design

2026-03-03 - QA: Background collector implemented with two policies: (a) adaptive-sample-by-error-rate and (b) tail-retention-on-spike. End-to-end functional test added. Note: need to harden when ring buffer is full to avoid blocking callers.

2026-03-06 - Perf team: Canary at 5% traffic for runtime-1.20 on staging. Observed CPU drop ~18% at 200k rps workload, p95 latency delta +0.7ms (within SLA). Memory allocations reduced by ~42%. Metrics dashboard: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/trace-minifier-canary

2026-03-09 - Security review request submitted. Initial findings: no PII extraction by default; minifier rules must be auditable. PR opened to add KMS-marking for full-span retention: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-minifier/pull/452

2026-03-10 - Ravi Patel: Preparing rollout plan. Next steps include hardened backpressure when ring buffer overflows, integrating with Dedicated runtime APIs, and creating a migration doc for SDKs. Planning a broader canary (25%) in 2026-03-17 if validation passes.
notes: Trade-offs: deferring span assembly increases complexity in background worker and requires robust failure modes (drop, best-effort resend). We must ensure the worker's CPU cost doesn't negate hotpath gains. Also need clear escape hatch for customers who rely on full spans in real time.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Hotpath microbench shows >10% CPU reduction on gateway under representative load. 2) End-to-end p95 latency change <= +2ms for canary traffic. 3) Background collector can recover from a 60s ring-buffer-full event without blocking callers. 4) Observability dashboards show new metrics (ring_buffer_fill, minifier_dropped_keys, sampled_tail_rate). 5) Security review approved and minifier rulebook documented on Confluence.
